- We fire off a preload fetch of _earlyRequest_. If it comes back before the document is created we set _earlyResponse_.

I think the spec right now will just do two duplicate fetches to the same URL, right? And whichever comes back later will override the entry in the map of preloaded resources.

> 
> * We fire off a preload fetch of _earlyRequest_. If it comes back before the document is created we set _earlyResponse_.

> Is there any interaction between any ongoing _earlyRequest_s and any link headers that come in after the status code, but before the document is created? I think the spec right now will just do two duplicate fetches to the same URL, right? And whichever comes back later will override the entry in the map of preloaded resources.

It's quite explicit in the PR actually.
See https://whatpr.org/html/7675/a54ae27...e6f2a97/browsing-the-web.html, create and initialize a Document object:

If there is an ongoing early request, it will be committed to the document in section 18 before the post-status link headers are processed in section 19. The post-status link headers will then fetch, which would find those responses in `consume a preloaded link`.

It would essentially be the same as having two preload link tags with the same href.
